title: Probability of Independent Events
description: Simple probability, multiplication rule, complements, and independent-event reasoning.

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed once. Find the probability of getting heads.
questions.explanation: A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes, so $P(H)=1/2$.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled once. Find the probability of getting a $4$.
questions.explanation: There is one favourable outcome out of six.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled once. Find the probability of getting an even number.
questions.explanation: The even outcomes are $2,4,6$, so probability is $3/6=1/2$.

questions.q: Two fair coins are tossed. Find the probability of getting two heads.
A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. Find the probability of heads and a $6$.
questions.explanation: The events are independent, so multiply: $1/2\times1/6=1/12$.

questions.q: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability of getting two sixes.
If $P(A)=\frac{2}{5}$ and $P(B)=\frac{3}{4}$ for independent events, find $P(A\cap B)$.
questions.explanation: For independent events, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)=2/5\times3/4=6/20=3/10$.

questions.q: If $P(A)=0.3$, find $P(A')$.
A bag has $3$ red and $2$ blue balls. One ball is picked at random. Find $P(blue)$.
questions.explanation: There are $2$ blue balls out of $5$ balls.

questions.q: A bag has $4$ red and $6$ green balls. A ball is picked, replaced, and another is picked. Find the probability both are red.
questions.explanation: With replacement, the events are independent: $4/10\times4/10=16/100=4/25$.

questions.q: What does it mean for two events to be independent?
options: One event changes the probability of the other.
One event does not affect the probability of the other.
questions.explanation: Independent events do not change each other's probabilities.

questions.q: If $P(A)=\frac14$ and $P(B)=\frac12$, independent, find $P(A\text{ and not }B)$.
A fair die is rolled twice. Find the probability of getting an odd number both times.
questions.explanation: Each roll has probability $3/6=1/2$ of odd, so both odd is $1/2\times1/2=1/4$.

questions.q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. Find the probability of drawing a heart.
questions.explanation: There are $13$ hearts out of $52$ cards, so $13/52=1/4$.

questions.q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. Find the probability of drawing an ace.
questions.explanation: There are $4$ aces out of $52$ cards, so $4/52=1/13$.

questions.q: A coin is tossed three times. Find the probability of getting all tails.
If the probability of rain is $0.2$, find the probability that it will not rain.
questions.explanation: The complement is $1-0.2=0.8$.

questions.q: A spinner has equal sectors numbered $1$ to $5$. Find the probability of landing on a number greater than $3$.
questions.explanation: The favourable outcomes are $4$ and $5$, so probability is $2/5$.

questions.q: Two independent events have probabilities $0.6$ and $0.5$. Find the probability that both occur.
questions.explanation: Multiply: $0.6\times0.5=0.3$.

questions.q: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability of getting a sum of $7$.
questions.explanation: The six favourable pairs are $(1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1)$, so probability is $6/36=1/6$.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled twice. Find the probability of no six appearing.
questions.explanation: Probability of no six on one roll is $5/6$, so on two rolls it is $5/6\times5/6=25/36$.

questions.q: A coin is tossed twice. Find the probability of at least one head.
questions.explanation: Use the complement: no heads is TT with probability $1/4$, so at least one head is $1-1/4=3/4$.

questions.q: A bag has $5$ black and $5$ white balls. A ball is picked, replaced, and another is picked. Find $P(white, then black)$.
If $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$, then $A$ and $B$ are:
questions.explanation: This product rule is the test for independence.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled. Find the probability of not getting a $1$.
questions.explanation: Five outcomes are not $1$, so probability is $5/6$.

questions.q: Two coins are tossed. Find the probability of exactly one head.
questions.explanation: The outcomes HT and TH are favourable, so $2/4=1/2$.

questions.q: A box has $2$ defective bulbs out of $10$. Find the probability of selecting a good bulb.
questions.explanation: There are $8$ good bulbs out of $10$, so $8/10=4/5$.

questions.q: If $P(A)=0$, event $A$ is:
questions.explanation: A probability of $0$ means the event cannot occur.

questions.q: If $P(A)=1$, event $A$ is:
questions.explanation: A probability of $1$ means the event must occur.

questions.q: Which value cannot be a probability?
questions.explanation: Probabilities must lie between $0$ and $1$ inclusive.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled and a fair coin is tossed. How many equally likely outcomes are there?
questions.explanation: There are $6$ die outcomes and $2$ coin outcomes, so $6\times2=12$.

questions.q: A password uses one letter from $A,B,C$ and one digit from $1,2,3,4$. How many outcomes are possible?
questions.explanation: Use the multiplication rule: $3\times4=12$.

questions.q: If two events are mutually exclusive and both have non-zero probability, are they independent?
questions.explanation: If one occurs, the other cannot occur, so the probability of the other changes.

questions.q: A bag has $3$ red and $7$ blue balls. With replacement, find the probability of drawing red twice.
A family has two children. Assuming boy and girl are equally likely, find the probability both are girls.
questions.explanation: The equally likely outcomes are BB, BG, GB, GG. Only GG works.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled twice. Find the probability that the first roll is $2$ and the second is greater than $4$.
A spinner has $8$ equal sectors, $3$ of which are red. Find $P(not red)$.
questions.explanation: Five of the eight sectors are not red.

questions.q: A coin is tossed four times. Find the probability of four heads.
A die is rolled once. Find $P($prime number$)$.
questions.explanation: Prime outcomes on a die are $2,3,5$, so $3/6=1/2$.

questions.q: If $P(A)=\frac35$, find the odds against $A$ as a probability of not $A$.
